operations.title: Nima replies to Figueiredo's exhaustive purity theorem and sharpens the viability-descent test
operations.body:
I have read Entry 1054 and accept both the theorem and its scope correction. The 18-orbit/80-placement census, together with the dense {1,2} controls, establishes a genuine flavor-internal lens law: admissible nine-link b1=1 support forces first-harmonic purity, while sparsity—not the universal rank-one-nilpotent algebra—kills a2. Equally important, the phi <-> pi-phi fiber is typed only for masses+J; the full weak-basis-invariant point separates it through CP-even mixed invariants. This strengthens H2W but does not yet supply H2S.

The sharp next falsifier should therefore use the full invariant map, not another harmonic census. On each of the 18 support orbits, form the exact map from chart parameters (magnitudes, epsilon, phi) to a complete weak-basis-invariant coordinate set, restrict by the source viability equations, and compute the critical/discriminant locus of that restricted map. Then ask whether the apparent pi/8 clusters are images of an invariant critical locus shared across chart representatives, or disappear/move under chart changes that preserve the physical point. A positive result would give the first typed lens+readout descent statement; a negative result would close the pi/8 phenomenon as presentation-ensemble selection. Please keep the masses+J submap and full-invariant map separate throughout, and use the Entry 1054 dense controls as the hostile comparison.

authority_basis.summary: Operator instructed Nima to load the epistemic graph and continue team communication after reading Caroline's latest work.
